conservation.condition_narrative: The work is generally planar, though it is very slightly cockled at the edges. The window mat is offset away from the work slightly to allow for the broad, slight, overall bow of the work. All media is securely attached, and there are no discolorations, holes, tears, or losses. There is a slight tape disturbance of the paper surface in the upper right corner. There are tiny, very isolated, black, pinpoint inclusions in the paper throughout. Paints have very sharply defined edges without liquid diffusion and are secure and stable. There are occasional, isolated, pinpoint transfers of blue watercolor. The work is hinged with wide Japanese mulberry fiber papers and methyl cellulose at three areas across the top edge and one each at the lower left and right corners of the bottom edge.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is very thick, white, rough-textured, wove paper. Watermarks are visible in the upper left and lower right corners, reading "VERITABLE PAPIER D'ACHES TORCHON [sic]." 
 
 
 
**Ground:** None. 
 
 
 
**Design Layers:** Large, wide watercolor brushwork, slightly overlapped, in minimal application of paint with strict control over paint density or value. Brushwork creates spatial relationships of simplified linear or geometric forms with no underdrawing. 
 
 
 
**Surface Coating:** No coating is discernible over the painting. Paper support may have been sized by the artist prior to painting to diminish absorption into the surface. This is occasionally suggested by the stiff overall hand, broad cockling, and odd absorption dullness of UV auto-fluorescence. 
 
 
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** New white-wash-finish maple with Optium optical titanium-coated, non-reflective, anti-static acrylic glazing. Work has 100% cotton rag, buffered Rising Museum Mounting backing, and window mats. Frame has basswood secondary backing, strainer, and acid-free Fome-Cor backing with "T-bolt" security hardware. The work is "cradled" on the verso with an oversized sheet of Mulberry-fiber paper, which is trimmed and folded to form an enclosed border around the margins of the work. The Mulberry-fiber paper is then mounted to the backing mat. No adhesive is used on the work of art.
